A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PBI-Attack and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D. Content can be reliably matched across pagination changes and relocated displays.

before.justification: v3 reports original attack-success, toxicity, efficiency, defense, and ablation results, including AdvBench evaluations and the HADES experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: v4 retains these original results and reports additional baseline, fixed-budget, defense, component-ablation, and initial-image experiments.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Equations 1–7 retain the same surrogate-derived visual prior and alternating greedy text/image optimization. The additional evaluations and initialization explanations do not revise the proposed attack procedure.

E1.justification: AdvBench and HADES coverage is retained. v4 adds evaluation with safety-system-prompt-protected targets and tests photographic versus random-noise initial images, extending input and target-environment scenarios within the existing jailbreak task.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds MLAI (Hao et al., 2024), evaluated across all six models. FigStep and HADES receive new baseline descriptions but already have reported results in v3. The HADES-dataset comparison retains its comparator set.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce common 5/10/20-hour budgets, a specified safety system prompt, Stage 1-only controls, and six initial-image conditions. Existing dataset settings, evaluation metrics, model sizes, and main optimization budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 substantially extends the analyses through fixed-budget efficiency comparisons (Table 7), system-prompt defense testing (Table 9), stage-contribution ablation (Table 11), and initial-image sensitivity testing (Table 12). These address distinct questions beyond v3's retained parameter sensitivities, prior-initialization comparison, and perturbation defense.

E5.justification: Both versions specify averaging ten responses per input pair and repeating experiments three times with means and standard deviations. No new statistical testing or uncertainty-estimation practice is introduced. The six seed images in Table 12 are input variations, not disclosed random-run seeds.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results are retained, but v4 substantially expands reported findings with MLAI scores and four new experimental tables. Table 7 shows PBI below UMK at 5/10 hours but above it at 20 hours; Table 9 reports PBI ASRs of 45.8% on MiniGPT-4 and 18.4% on GPT-4 under the added defense. Tables 11–12 add stage and initial-image results. These are additional conditions, not revisions of the original benchmark scores. Appendix D.1 also removes cautionary and awareness-raising portions of displayed responses.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, threat assumptions, loss, and update equations remain unchanged. Neither version adds formal propositions, proofs, or derivations beyond the retained method formulation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same prior-guided bimodal black-box attack and superiority claims, including the 92.5% and 67.3% headline averages. Added experiments support the existing contribution rather than redefine it.

C2.justification: v3 justifies greater computational cost through final ASR; v4 adds a budget-dependent interpretation, emphasizing comparable performance at 10 hours and a higher ceiling at 20 hours. Appendix B newly attributes gains to both stages and argues that initial-image choice is non-critical. The limitations section remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code-availability statement and repository location, explicitly identifies the default panda image and alternative image types, and supplies the complete defense system prompt. Existing hardware and principal hyperparameter disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: The cited literature is substantially broadened with MLAI and additional work on multimodal attacks, robustness, alignment, bias mitigation, and multimodal modeling. These are newly cited works, although the central comparison with prior methods and the novelty argument remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 revises the author and affiliation block, adds acknowledgments and baseline descriptions, expands the efficiency and defense discussion, and shortens Appendix D.1 examples. Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds Tables 7, 9, 11, and 12 and an MLAI row in Table 1. Figure 3 moves from page 6 to page 8, and the retained perturbation-defense table becomes a larger display. All ten figures retain their artwork, axes, and legends; other changes mainly involve reflow and renumbering.

improvement.justification: Compared with v3's cost reporting, v4's common-budget comparison better supports assessment of efficiency, while the added defense and stage/image controls strengthen empirical scrutiny. The code-location disclosure also improves reproducibility information. These gains are tempered by insufficiently explained new ablation conditions and unmarked removal of cautionary and awareness-raising passages from Appendix D.1 outputs, supporting a limited net improvement.
